title: Examination of a supplement to manage mood and brain activity in women with premenstrual dysphoric disorder (extreme emotional, behavioral, and physical symptoms in the 1 to 2 weeks before a period)
official: Examination of a supplement to manage mood and brain activity in women with premenstrual dysphoric disorder
summary:
Background and study aims
Premenstrual dysphoric disorder (PMDD) is a severe condition that can cause anxiety, depression, mood changes and other emotional and physical symptoms in the one to two weeks before a menstrual period. Current treatments do not work well for everyone and can sometimes cause unwanted side effects.
Researchers want to find out whether a nutritional supplement called Ditto can reduce anxiety and other PMDD symptoms, improve wellbeing, and help people manage their emotions better. The study will also investigate whether the supplement affects brain activity linked to mood by using a test called electroencephalography (EEG), which records the brain's electrical activity.

Who can participate?
Women aged 18 to 45 years can take part if they have a diagnosis of PMDD, or believe they have PMDD, and have symptoms that meet the study's eligibility requirements. People who are pregnant or breastfeeding, taking certain medicines, have some neurological, psychiatric or bowel conditions, or have allergies to ingredients in the supplement will not be able to take part.

What does the study involve?
The study will include 100 participants. Each participant will be randomly assigned to receive either the Ditto supplement or a placebo (dummy treatment) that looks the same but contains no active ingredients expected to affect mood or brain function. Neither the participants nor the researchers will know which treatment has been allocated until the study has finished.
Participants will take two capsules by mouth each day for three menstrual cycles, which is about 12 weeks.
At the start of the study, participants will attend a three-hour visit at Queen Mary University of London. During this visit they will complete questionnaires about their health, mood, diet, physical activity and other experiences. They will also have an EEG assessment.
During the 12-week study period, participants will complete online questionnaires once each week. These questionnaires will ask about PMDD symptoms, anxiety, depression, quality of life and any side effects. Completing the questionnaires will take about 15 minutes each week.
At the end of the study, participants will attend a second three-hour visit to repeat some of the questionnaires and the EEG assessment.

What are the possible benefits and risks of participating?
Participants may experience an improvement in their PMDD symptoms, although this cannot be guaranteed. The information collected may help researchers develop new treatment options for people with PMDD in the future.
The risks of taking part are expected to be low. The supplement contains nutrients that are commonly found in foods, although some people may experience mild stomach upset. EEG is a safe and painless procedure. Some questionnaire questions about mood and past experiences may be upsetting for some people. Participants can choose not to answer questions, take breaks, or withdraw from the study at any time.

Where is the study run from?
The study is run from Queen Mary University of London, United Kingdom.

When is the study starting and how long is it expected to run for?
November 2026 to June 2028.

Who is funding the study?
The study is funded by Ditto Daily and Queen Mary University of London through a match-funded PhD studentship.

Who is the main contact?
Dr Paul Faulkner, p.faulkner@qmul.ac.uk

interventions.name: One hundred women with PMDD will be randomly allocated to one of two parallel arms. Participants will be randomised in a 1:1 ratio to the intervention or placebo arm using a computer-generated randomisation sequence (block randomisation). This is a double-blind trial: participants and the researcher

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1.	Aged 18 to 45 years
2.	Assigned female at birth
3.	Self-reporting premenstrual dysphoric disorder (PMDD) or having a clinical diagnosis of PMDD
4.	Scoring 70 or above out of 144 on the 24-item Daily Record of Severity of Problems (DRSP) during the luteal phase of the menstrual cycle
Exclusion criteria:
1.	Consuming more than 10 units of alcohol per week
2.	Having a history of illicit drug use, drug abuse, or addiction
3.	Currently using nicotine or tobacco
4.	Having a neurological condition
5.	Having any psychiatric condition other than premenstrual dysphoric disorder (PMDD)
6.	Being pregnant or breastfeeding
7.	Currently using antidepressants, including selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs)
8.	Currently using hormonal therapy for PMDD
9.	Currently using medication for attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD)
10.	Regularly using sedatives, benzodiazepines, or sleep medication
11.	Currently using antibiotics
12.	Currently using levothyroxine
13.	Currently using bisphosphonates, including alendronate, risedronate, or ibandronate
14.	Having an allergy or sensitivity to chamomile or ragweed (Asteraceae/Compositae family)
15.	Having an allergy or sensitivity to saffron, zinc, or any other ingredient of the study supplement
16.	Having irritable bowel syndrome
17.	Having inflammatory bowel disease
18.	Having Crohn’s disease
19.	Having coeliac disease
20.	Having haemochromatosis
21.	Previous use of the study supplement Ditto
